title: MCX Options Trading: Lot Sizes, Expiry and Crude Oil Examples
summary: Learn how MCX options work, with lot sizes, crude oil premium examples, Gold vs Gold Mini, expiry rules and ways to practise and backtest strategies.
body_markdown:
MCX options are European-style options on commodity futures traded on the Multi Commodity Exchange of India. A call gives its buyer the right to take a long futures position at the strike price; a put gives the right to take a short futures position. Exercised options become futures positions, which require futures margin.


You can trade options on crude oil, natural gas, gold, silver, copper and zinc. Before placing a trade, check the exact contract, its lot size (the number of units the premium is multiplied by), expiry and settlement method.


**Quick answer: how MCX options work**


-


One option lot corresponds to one lot of its underlying futures contract.


-


Buyers pay the premium upfront; sellers need margin. Buyers may also need devolvement margin near expiry.


-


Options can be bought or sold before expiry, subject to liquidity and broker restrictions. European-style means they can only be exercised at expiry.


-


Options expire before their underlying futures. Crude oil and natural gas options expire two business days earlier, and Gold Mini and copper options expire three business days before the futures’ tender period begins.


-


ITM options are normally exercised automatically unless the long holder submits a valid contrary instruction. OTM options expire worthless.


-


Energy futures are cash-settled; the metal futures covered below can lead to physical delivery.

## How MCX Options Differ From Nifty and Sensex Options


MCX options use a commodity futures price to determine moneyness, rather than a spot index. Exercised options become futures positions, while Nifty and Sensex index options settle in cash.


MCX commodity options also trade into the evening. Normal sessions for the contracts above run from 9 AM to 11:30 PM or 11:55 PM IST, depending on the seasonal schedule. Check[MCX trading timings](https://algotest.in/blog/mcx-trading-time/) and your broker’s earlier square-off cutoffs.


To compare strikes, open interest, volume and IV, read our[MCX option chain guide](https://algotest.in/blog/how-to-read-mcx-option-chain/) . Check liquidity in the exact option you want to trade; an active futures contract does not guarantee an active option strike.


## Crude Oil Options: Premium and P&L Example


One Crude Oil option lot covers 100 barrels. If a call trades at ₹120 per barrel, buying one lot costs ₹120 × 100 = ₹12,000, before charges.


If you close that position before expiry:

This P&L follows the change in the option premium. A ₹30 move in crude oil futures does not necessarily produce a ₹30 change in the option premium. Time remaining, volatility and the strike also affect its price.


At the same ₹120 premium, one Crude Oil Mini option lot costs ₹1,200 because it covers 10 barrels. Actual standard and mini premiums can differ. See our[Crude Oil and Crude Oil Mini lot size](https://algotest.in/blog/crude-oil-lot-size/) guide for the exposure calculation.


## Trading Crude Oil Options Around EIA Data


The US Energy Information Administration normally publishes its Weekly Petroleum Status Report on Wednesdays at 10:30 AM Eastern. Its natural-gas storage report normally follows on Thursdays at the same time.


US time regime


Normal 10:30 AM Eastern release in India


Daylight saving time


8 PM IST


Standard time


9 PM IST


Holiday schedules can change both the day and time. For example, the petroleum report scheduled for 12 November 2026 is at noon Eastern, or 10:30 PM IST. Check the[EIA petroleum release calendar](https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/schedule.php) and natural-gas release calendar before planning a trade.


Around a release:


-


A drop in implied volatility can reduce an option’s premium even if the futures price moves in the buyer’s expected direction.


-


Option sellers face the risk of a sharp move. A higher premium does not make the position safer.


-


Spreads can widen. A limit order controls your acceptable execution price, but may remain unfilled.

## MCX Option Expiry and Devolvement


Options expire before their underlying futures. Crude oil and natural-gas options generally expire two business days before their futures. Gold Mini and copper options expire three business days before the underlying futures’ tender period begins. Always use the listed expiry for your exact contract.

## What Happens When an Option Is Exercised?


Devolvement means an exercised option becomes a position in its underlying futures contract.


Option position


Futures position on exercise or assignment


Long call


Long futures


Short call


Short futures


Long put


Short futures


Short put


Long futures


Devolved futures positions are opened at the option’s strike price. ITM options are normally exercised automatically unless the long holder submits a valid contrary instruction. OTM options expire worthless. If the strike equals the settlement price exactly, the option also expires worthless.


**CTM clarification:** MCX discontinued the old close-to-the-money exercise category for contracts launched from 1 February 2022. Brokers may still use “CTM” to calculate margin, but that does not mean near-ATM options require an explicit exercise request.


## Margin and Delivery After Devolvement


A futures position needs futures margin. Brokers may block devolvement margin before option expiry and close positions that do not meet their funding rules. Zerodha’s October bulletin, for example, specifies 100% futures margin for NRML ITM long options and 50% for its CTM long-option category on expiry day.


Cash-settled crude oil and natural-gas futures do not require physical delivery. Gold, silver, copper and zinc futures can create delivery obligations during the tender period or at expiry. After devolvement, further futures losses can exceed the original option premium.


#### Before-Expiry Checklist


1.


Confirm the option expiry and underlying futures contract.


2.


Check your broker’s margin and square-off deadlines.


3.


Decide whether to close, roll or retain the position before those deadlines.


4.


If retaining it, understand futures funding and settlement obligations.


5.


For deliverable futures, check the tender-period start date.


Include these checks in your[trading risk-management plan](https://algotest.in/blog/trading-risk-management-rules-examples-and-a-practical-plan/) .


## Margin and Charges for MCX Options


Buyers pay the full premium upfront and may need additional funds near expiry. Sellers need risk-based margin. Eligible hedges can reduce margin, but the benefit depends on the exact legs and the applicable rules. Confirm the requirement with your broker before placing or changing a position. Our[MCX margin](https://algotest.in/blog/mcx-margin/) guide explains how margin is set.


Charges include brokerage, exchange fees, SEBI charges, GST, stamp duty and applicable Commodities Transaction Tax (CTT):


-


**Sale of an option on commodity futures:** CTT is 0.05% of the premium transaction value, payable by the seller.


-


**Exercise of an option on commodity futures:** CTT is 0.0001% of the settlement-price-based transaction value, payable by the purchaser.


These are separate taxable events. Transaction value accounts for contract quantity and quotation units; it is not simply the displayed per-unit price. Further futures transactions can attract their own charges. Refer to[MCXCCL’s CTT schedule](https://www.mcxccl.com/clearing-settlement/commodities-transaction-tax) .

### FAQs


#### What are MCX options?


MCX options are European-style options on commodity futures, such as crude oil, natural gas, gold, silver, copper and zinc. A call gives the right to take a long futures position at the strike price, and a put gives the right to take a short futures position.


#### When do MCX options expire?


MCX options expire before their underlying futures. Crude oil and natural gas options generally expire two business days before their futures, and Gold Mini and copper options three business days before the futures’ tender period begins. Always check the listed expiry for your contract.


#### What is devolvement in MCX options?


Devolvement is when an exercised option turns into a position in its underlying futures at the strike price. In-the-money options are exercised automatically unless the holder opts out, so you need futures margin, and for gold, silver, copper and zinc the position can lead to delivery.


#### Can I sell an MCX option before expiry?


Yes, you can generally close a bought option by selling the same contract before expiry, subject to liquidity and broker restrictions. European-style limits when it can be exercised, not when it can be traded.


#### How much does one Crude Oil option lot cost?


Multiply the quoted premium per barrel by 100. At ₹120, one standard lot costs ₹12,000 before charges. A Crude Oil Mini lot covers 10 barrels, so the same premium quote gives a ₹1,200 cost.


#### Are MCX option buyers’ losses limited to the premium?


A standalone long option can lose its premium plus charges. However, if it is exercised into futures and you retain that position, further futures losses can exceed the original premium. Check devolvement and margin rules before expiry.


#### Is Gold Mini always one-tenth the price of Gold options?


Only when comparing the same quoted premium per 10 grams. Gold Mini’s lot size is one-tenth of Gold’s, but actual premiums differ with the underlying futures, expiry and liquidity.


#### What time is EIA crude oil data released in India?


The normal Wednesday release is at 8 PM IST during US daylight saving time and 9 PM IST during standard time. Holiday releases can have a different day and time, so check EIA’s petroleum calendar.
